title: Burst forensics and dispute reconciliation workflow
creator: Marco Liu
description:
Problem statement: When tenants consume burst/surge capacity (surge pools or temporary boosts) and then dispute the resulting invoice or request SLA credits, operators lack a concise, reproducible artifact to explain what happened. Current billing pipelines aggregate at the tenant-window level and lose per-request metadata needed to reconcile KV-cache effects, per-request queuing, and fallback to cheaper model variants. This makes customer conversations slow, increases refund risk, and drives engineering time on ad-hoc analysis.

Goal: Build an operator-friendly 'burst forensics' workflow and minimal preserved telemetry so disputes can be resolved quickly and accurately. The workflow should enable: 1) reconstruction of per-route token consumption and model-variant selection for a configurable window around the surge, 2) automatic identification of burst origin signals (traffic spike vs. routing fallback vs. autoscale gap), 3) a repeatable dispute reconciliation playbook that results in either automatic grace credits or a human-approved adjustment, and 4) a low-cost retention model with privacy safeguards.

Acceptance criteria (must pass QA):
- For any billing dispute opened within 21 days, operators can produce a repeatable report covering the 6-hour window around the peak with per-request token counts, model variant used, queue wait time, and whether request hit prefix/KV cache.
- The report includes an automated heuristic classification of root cause (traffic surge, transient capacity shortage, routing fallback, client-retry storm) with confidence score.
- If the heuristic classifies an event as "transient boost artifact" with >= 90% confidence and tenant meets entitlement rules, system can propose an automated grace credit amount and apply pending operator approval.
- Storage and retention controls are configurable per-tenant and default to a 21-day retention for forensics traces.
- All preserved traces are encrypted at rest and logged to audit trail when accessed for dispute handling.

Deliverables:
- Data contract for the minimal forensics artifact (timestamped request id, tenant id, route, model_variant, token_input_count, token_output_count, kv_cache_hit boolean, queue_ms, node_id, admission_policy, surge_pool_id if applicable).
- ETL that can reconstruct the 6-hour window report from existing high-volume logs + small additional per-request capture flag.
- Operator UI panel in Console -> Dedicated -> Incidents -> Burst Forensics that shows generated reports and allows applying proposed credits.
- Playbook doc (Confluence) describing steps for dispute intake, escalation, and audit sign-off.
- Automated tests and a runbook for on-call when forensics pipeline fails to generate a report.

Proposed technical approach and trade-offs:
- Minimal capture: instead of full payloads, capture only the forensics artifact fields listed above. This limits storage and PII exposure (no prompt text stored by default).
- Sampling policy: default to persist 100% of requests while a tenant is in a detected surge window (to ensure reproducibility). Outside surge windows use 1% sample and keep aggregated counters. Surge detection uses existing surge-pool controller signals + short-term rolling delta on RPS.
- Retention: default 21 days; tenant-level override up to 90 days for enterprise contracts. Longer retention requires explicit opt-in and legal review.
- Encryption & access: artifacts encrypted with tenant-specific KMS keys where available. Access gated via Console RBAC and logged.
- Cost vs fidelity trade-off: full payload retention would make disputes trivial but increases storage and compliance burden. The chosen minimal artifact balances operator needs and cost.

Instrumentation changes needed:
- Add a compact forensics envelope at request admission in the serving runtime. Flag included in request trace metadata if 'forensics capture' active.
- Modify batching layer to propagate forensics flags so that per-request pairing to token accounting remains stable despite batching/continuous inference.
- Small changes to billing ETL to accept per-request deltas and attribute them to surge pools/temporary boosts vs committed capacity.

Operator workflow and UI:
- New Console panel lists active/recent surge windows with an "Open Forensics Report" action.
- Report shows timeline chart (RPS, queue times, model variant distribution), top N request patterns, and suggested classification + credit amount with rationale.
- Operators can download a signed report PDF and trigger a credit action with templated customer email matching legal-approved language.

Billing and entitlement rules (initial draft):
- Automatic grace credit can be proposed when: (a) spike duration < 30 minutes, (b) > 80% of excess tokens attributable to a routing fallback or autoscale gap, (c) tenant not in trial/abuse flags, (d) tenant has <= 2 prior disputes in 90 days.
- Credit calculation: prorate excess tokens above committed capacity for the spike window, cap credit at 75% of excess cost, and mark for operator review before applying.

Security & compliance notes:
- Forensic artifacts intentionally exclude prompt content to reduce data leakage. If a customer requires full payload retention for forensic purposes it must be a separately negotiated term with security review and opt-in.
- All access to artifacts requires an audit trail entry. Admin role must justify access reason (dispute id / ticket id).

Open questions / risks:
- How to handle multi-tenant nodes where node_id correlation could leak co-tenancy signals? Mitigation: obfuscate node identifiers in operator-facing reports.
- Memory and storage cost estimates for worst-case sustained surges: needs capacity planning with Infra to ensure ETL can materialize 6-hour windows for multiple concurrent tenants.
- Accuracy of classification heuristics: may require ML model trained on labeled past incidents; initial rules-based heuristics may have false positives.

Links / artifacts:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.internal/dedicated-capacity/burst-forensics (draft)
- Design mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1BF-burst-forensics-ui
- GitHub draft PR (instrumentation): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7654
- Billing ETL spike attribution prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/finance/tree/feature/burst-attrib

Next steps (short-term plan):
- Week 1: finalize forensics artifact schema and secure approvals from security and finance (owners: Marco, Priya). Create BOM for storage cost.
- Week 2-3: implement lightweight capture flag and minimal envelope in serving runtime; add batching propagation hooks (owner: Evelyn).
- Week 4: ETL prototype that reconstructs reports from a replayed surge from telemetry; smoke test with synthetic load.
- Week 5: Console UI with download and credit action wired to a sandbox billing queue.
- Week 6: Pilot with two enterprise customers who opt-in; iterate on heuristics and UI.

If successful this significantly reduces time-to-resolution for disputes and lowers refund risk while providing clearer SLAs around burst behavior.
